correctness.rationale: Every selected point has barycentric mass with sum (n-1)/n at each vertex; no simplex vertex can occur. If the n-vertex support multigraph (n-1 chosen edge points) were disconnected, a component of k between 1 and n-1 vertices would contain k(n-1)/n edges, impossible by integrality and gcd(n,n-1)=1. Hence it is a simple spanning tree. A cut isolates k-1 other edge points; their barycentric mass forces the unique fractions (n-k)/n and k/n. The converse holds because the branches of each vertex partition the remaining n-1 vertices. Distinct edge supports yield distinct sets and Cayley gives n^(n-2). For a regular simplex, centered Gram coordinates give squared radial displacement; sum of k(n-k) across tree cuts is the Wiener index, and the zero-mean pairwise polarization identity yields the stated energy. Elementary sharp Wiener bounds with equality give paths at the energy minimum and stars at the maximum (n=3 overlap). Independent exact-rational reconstruction tested all 1440 labeled trees at n=3,4,5,6, confirming each cut weight, centroid, Wiener sum, direct pairwise energy, extrema and multiplicities; finite checks corroborate but cannot prove the universal result.
residual_risks: The source proof relies on classical Cayley enumeration and standard Wiener extrema; needed latter equality cases are independently shown.
No general n is inferred from the finite enumeration; general proof is analytic.

value.rationale: Balancing equal point masses on a polytope one-skeleton is a published geometric problem. Its canonical simplex-centroid instance admits a complete all-dimensional classification of every solution, explicit tree-cut barycentric positions and exactly n^(n-2) distinct sets. Summed squared pairwise separation is a natural regular-simplex configuration statistic; identifying it exactly with the tree Wiener index transfers substantive path/star rigidity to Euclidean geometry. This motivated exact family result is not merely an isolated table, renaming of Cayley or a minor gain; it is useful without requiring an additional downstream theorem.
residual_risks: The metric classification applies only to regular simplices and the special number/weights/target of balancing points.
